title: A three-month pressure index gave no clear six-month ENSO forecast gain at 2000-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether the trailing three-month Southern Oscillation Index improves six-month forecasts of monthly Nino 3.4 anomalies beyond seasonal surface temperature history. We used fixed NOAA CPC SOI and ERSSTv5 snapshots, yearly time-ordered fits, and 300 test origins in 2000-2024. Added pressure terms raised mean squared error by 0.13%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was -1.25% to 1.21%. Root mean squared error changed from 0.65875 C to 0.65919 C. All five planned model checks also had intervals that included zero. This gives no clear added forecast gain for these terms. It does not show that atmospheric coupling is absent. Revised indices, rounded values, model form, 25 test years and conditional uncertainty limit the result. The package contains code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, numerical checks and a figure. Raw data and row-level regeneration stay in external scratch.

display.caption: Monthly forecast error, all planned comparisons and cumulative paired annual error. Intervals are conditional 95% three-year block intervals.

citations.reason: Prior benchmark informed the seasonal surface controls. We reuse the same SST snapshot with new code and test SOI. Data overlap.
Prior pressure-based predictor differs from SOI; its reported gain motivates this narrower benchmark.
